text:
maria: Heads-up — ran into a kernel-selection oddity on SM86 with Flash/SDPA where head_dim=14 picks sdpa_v3_causal then falls back to the naive kernel and ends up 2.4x slower for seqlen=256.

tom: repro steps? config?

maria: quick repro:
```
# python snippet
run_infer --model redwood/7B --device cuda:0 --seqlen 256 --batch 1 --head-dim 14 --causal True --warmup 3
```
Log: 
```
[2025-11-03 09:12:11] kernel_picker: probed sdpa_v3_causal (score=0.62)
[2025-11-03 09:12:11] kernel_picker: selected sdpa_v3_causal
[2025-11-03 09:12:11] sdpa_v3_causal: runtime error, falling back
[2025-11-03 09:12:11] kernel_picker: fallback to naive_sdp (score=0.10)
```
Perf numbers (from perf-bot): sdpa_v3_causal expected ~12ms/token, actual flow ended up ~32ms/token. naive_sdp is ~28ms/token.

kevin: this smells like the microprobe/warmup probing choosing a variant that triggers a slow code path (maybe misaligned tile) and then falling back but with extra overhead (reallocation/streams). Does the fallback path insert extra copy or kv cache flush?

sara: i saw similar when head_dim not a multiple of 16 — some optimized kernels assume head stride padding and hit a slow scalar loop. Could be a vectorization miss in v3.

maria: adding more detail — this happened only when using prefix KV cache (streaming chat). Without KV cache, sdpa_v3 stays and is fast. With KV cache, the v3 probe returns OK but then runtime detects a causal-pad mismatch and bails.

perf-bot: profile dump attached:
```
# condensed timeline
alloc(cuda) 1.6ms
kernel_launch(sdpa_v3) 0.8ms
sync/check 4.2ms -> error path
alloc(copy) 2.1ms
naive_kernel 25.6ms
```
Memory charts show small repeated allocations around the probe/verify step.

tom: do we have device-specific repro? SM86 only? SM90?

maria: repro on SM86 and SM80. SM90 seems to avoid the verify error (likely because of different alignment helpers). So it's not only SM86 but more common on older arch.

kevin: theory: v3's causal fastpath expects packed KV layout (head_stride % 32 == 0) when using cached KV. The probe didn't validate cached layout, only runtime verify detected mismatch. When verify fails we pay cost of attempted launch + sync, then fallback.

maria: confirmed by instrumenting verify: it returns false for head_stride=14 -> triggers fallback.

sara: immediate mitigations:
- (1) change probe heuristics to reject kernels if head_dim % warp_width != 0 when KV cache enabled; cheaper than trying launch.
- (2) add a short-circuit check for cached KV layout before choosing v3.
- (3) extend warmup to include a quick non-timed validate pass (no launch) to avoid sync overhead.

tom: sounds good. Any concerns about regressing cases where v3 would actually be fine? we'll lose some wins if heuristics too strict.

kevin: can add a soft-probe flag to prefer existing behavior but collect telemetry for mismatches. If heuristics cut actual wins <1% we can relax.

perf-bot: telemetry: over last 2 weeks, 0.7% of requests hit this head-dim mismatch pattern, but they account for ~6% of slow tail latencies on dedicated pools with streaming enabled.

maria: proposed patch: kernel_picker: before probe, if (kv_cache_enabled && head_dim % 16 != 0) mark v3 as "needs_strict_verify" and do a pre-verify check on layout, avoid launch+sync. I'll draft PR.

sara: also add a sequence-length bucket rule: for seqlen in [128,512], prefer v2 non-causal when head_dim < 16 — avoids v3 micro-alloc penalties.

tom: can we get a quick canary: change picker logic behind a config flag rollout to dedicated clusters? then measure tail latency for streaming routes.

maria: plan:
- PR: pre-verify and soft-probe flag (maria)
- Canary: config flag behind rollout (tom)
- Telemetry dashboard: bucket by head_dim, seqlen, kv_enabled (kevin)
- Follow-up: microbenchmark suite to include head_dim odd sizes (sara)

infra-bot: deploy job queued: redwood/infra/canary/2025-11-03-18:00

kevin: one more ask — add a small unit test that simulates cached KV with odd head stride and asserts picker marks v3 as needs_verify. Avoid full kernel launch in CI.

maria: yep. I'll include that in the PR and attach the perf-bot summary after canary.

tom: thanks — this explains a mysterious regression. :thumbsup:

sara: fyi, filing a short docs note about "head-dim alignment gotchas" so solutions are discoverable by infra teams.

maria: assigning follow-ups in the PR. Will paste links here when ready.

perf-bot: summary metric pre-canary vs target: tail p99 latency for streaming routes down to expected - target 12ms/token, current 28-32ms/token. Canary target: reduce tail to <18ms/token for affected buckets.

maria: thanks everyone, will post PR + canary results.
